explanation: Real periodic data — like temperature over a day — can be modeled by a sinusoid you tune by hand. The green dots are the measured readings; slide the four controls until the blue cosine rides through them. The midline is the average value, amplitude is half the high-to-low swing, the period is how long before the pattern repeats (24 h here), and peak is the time the curve reaches its maximum. The sweeping dot reads off the model's prediction at each hour.
bullets: midline = average of the high and low; amplitude = half their difference.
period is the time for one full cycle; peak sets WHEN the maximum occurs.
A good model is the curve that threads through all the data points at once.
